Pointblank's built-in support for JSON Schema, Frictionless Table Schema, dbt, and the Open Data Contract Standard is made of four `ContractAdapter` subclasses. Writing another subclass adds a new format, such as an organization's own data dictionary or a schema format from another tool. Once it's registered with [`register_adapter()`](`pointblank.register_adapter`), the new format works everywhere the built-in ones do. A subclass sets a few class attributes and implements up to three methods: - [`detect()`](`pointblank.ContractAdapter.detect`) decides whether a source is in this format, which lets `import_contract()` find the adapter without being told `format=` (optional) - [`import_contract()`](`pointblank.ContractAdapter.import_contract`) reads a source and returns a [`ContractImport`](`pointblank.ContractImport`) whose rules are expressed as [`MappedConstraint`](`pointblank.adapters.MappedConstraint`) objects (needed for import) - [`export_contract()`](`pointblank.ContractAdapter.export_contract`) translates a [`Contract`](`pointblank.Contract`) or [`Validate`](`pointblank.Validate`) object into the format (needed for export) The base class versions of these methods raise `NotImplementedError`. An adapter that only goes in one direction should set `supports_import` or `supports_export` to `False`, so that the unsupported direction fails with a clear error message. ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [format_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The name of the format, used as the value of `format=`. It's also the registration name when `register_adapter()` is used without one. [file_extensions]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : File name endings that identify the format, such as `[".schema.json"]`. They're matched against file paths during format detection, before any `detect()` method is tried. [supports_import]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Whether the adapter can import. The default is `True`. [supports_export]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Whether the adapter can export. The default is `True`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Suppose a team documents its tables in a "data dictionary" format of its own: a dictionary with the table name under `data_dictionary` and a list of `columns`. Each column has a name and a type and can say whether it's nullable, whether it's unique, and which values are allowed. It can also have a `pii` flag, which matters for governance but isn't a data quality rule. The adapter below supports both directions. Importing maps the column properties to `MappedConstraint` objects and records a warning for the `pii` flag, which has no equivalent. Exporting goes the other way, starting from a contract's schema and steps. ::: {#4e40b2b6 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import json import pointblank as pb from pointblank.adapters import MappedConstraint TYPES = {"integer": "Int64", "decimal": "Float64", "text": "String"} @pb.register_adapter class DataDictionaryAdapter(pb.ContractAdapter): format_name = "data_dictionary" file_extensions = [".dd.json"] @staticmethod def detect(source): return isinstance(source, dict) and "data_dictionary" in source def import_contract(self, source, **kwargs): path = None if isinstance(source, str): path = source with open(source) as f: source = json.load(f) columns, constraints, warnings = [], [], [] for fld in source["columns"]: name = fld["name"] columns.append((name, TYPES.get(fld.get("type")))) if fld.get("nullable") is False: constraints.append( MappedConstraint("col_vals_not_null", {"columns": name}, "nullable: false") ) if fld.get("unique"): constraints.append( MappedConstraint("rows_distinct", {"columns_subset": [name]}, "unique") ) if "allowed" in fld: constraints.append( MappedConstraint( "col_vals_in_set", {"columns": name, "set": fld["allowed"]}, "allowed" ) ) if fld.get("pii"): warnings.append(f"Column '{name}': the pii flag has no Pointblank equivalent.") n_rules = len(constraints) + len(warnings) return pb.ContractImport( source_format=self.format_name, source_path=path, columns=columns, constraints=constraints, metadata={"title": source["data_dictionary"]}, warnings=warnings, coverage=len(constraints) / n_rules if n_rules else 1.0, ) def export_contract(self, validation_or_contract, destination=None, **kwargs): if not isinstance(validation_or_contract, pb.Contract): raise TypeError("This adapter can only export a Contract.") contract = validation_or_contract to_dd_type = {pb_type: dd_type for dd_type, pb_type in TYPES.items()} entries = {name: {"name": name} for name, _ in contract.schema.columns} for name, dtype in contract.schema.columns: entries[name]["type"] = to_dd_type.get(dtype, "text") for step in contract.steps: columns = step.kwargs.get("columns") columns = [columns] if isinstance(columns, str) else columns or [] for col in columns: if step.method == "col_vals_not_null": entries[col]["nullable"] = False elif step.method == "col_vals_in_set": entries[col]["allowed"] = list(step.kwargs["set"]) doc = {"data_dictionary": contract.name, "columns": list(entries.values())} if destination is not None: with open(destination, "w") as f: json.dump(doc, f, indent=2) return doc ``` ::: The bare `@pb.register_adapter` decorator registered the class under its `format_name`. Now a data dictionary can be imported with `import_contract()`, and its `detect()` method means there's no need for `format=`. ::: {#b9f8cd98 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} customers_dd = { "data_dictionary": "customers", "columns": [ {"name": "customer_id", "type": "integer", "nullable": False, "unique": True}, {"name": "tier", "type": "text", "allowed": ["bronze", "silver", "gold"]}, {"name": "email", "type": "text", "nullable": False, "pii": True}, ], } imported = pb.import_contract(customers_dd) print(imported.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Contract Import Summary Format: data_dictionary Columns detected: 3 Constraints mapped: 4 Coverage: 80% Warnings (1): - Column 'email': the pii flag has no Pointblank equivalent. ``` ::: ::: Four of the five column properties became constraints and the `pii` flag became a warning, which the coverage figure reflects. From here the import behaves like any other: it can be validated against a table, turned into a contract, or written out as code. Exporting runs in the other direction. A contract written in Pointblank can be shared as a data dictionary with `export_contract()`. ::: {#3380da15 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} orders_contract = pb.Contract( name="orders", schema=pb.Schema(order_id="Int64", status="String", total="Float64"), steps=[ pb.Step("col_vals_not_null", columns=["order_id", "status"]), pb.Step("col_vals_in_set", columns="status", set=["open", "closed"]), pb.Step("col_vals_ge", columns="total", value=0), ], ) print(json.dumps(pb.export_contract(orders_contract, format="data_dictionary"), indent=2)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` { "data_dictionary": "orders", "columns": [ { "name": "order_id", "type": "integer", "nullable": false }, { "name": "status", "type": "text", "nullable": false, "allowed": [ "open", "closed" ] }, { "name": "total", "type": "decimal" } ] } ``` ::: ::: The schema supplied the columns and their types, and the not-null and set-membership steps became `nullable` and `allowed` properties. The data dictionary format has nothing that corresponds to `col_vals_ge()`, so that step was left out. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~register_adapter`) : Register an adapter so that it can be used by name. [](`~ContractImport`) : The object an adapter's `import_contract()` method returns. [](`~adapters.MappedConstraint`) : The objects that hold translated rules. [](`~list_adapters`) : List the registered adapters. ## Methods {.doc-methods} | Name | Description | |---|---| | [detect()](#detect){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Decide whether a source is in this adapter's format. | | [import_contract()](#import_contract){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Read a source in this format and translate it into Pointblank terms. | | [export_contract()](#export_contract){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Translate a Pointblank contract or validation into this format. | : {.gd-summary-table} ### [detect()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Decide whether a source is in this adapter's format. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/adapters/_base.py#L911-L973){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature detect(source) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} When [`import_contract()`](`pointblank.import_contract`) is called without `format=` and the source isn't a file path ending in one of the registered `file_extensions`, it calls `detect()` on each registered adapter in turn (in the order they were registered) and uses the first one that returns `True`. Implementing `detect()` lets users import a definition without having to name its format. A good `detect()` method looks for a feature that sets the format apart, such as a particular top-level key, and returns `False` for anything else. It's called on sources meant for other adapters too, so it should be quick and shouldn't assume anything about the source's type. When the source is a file path, check that the file exists before reading it. An exception raised in `detect()` is treated the same as returning `False`. Implementing this method is optional. The base class version raises `NotImplementedError`, which also counts as `False`, so an adapter without it can still be used by passing `format=`. The method must be a static method. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The `source=` value given to `import_contract()`: usually a file path string or a dictionary, but it could be any object. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if this adapter should import the source, `False` otherwise. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} This adapter recognizes its format by a `column_rules` key that holds a list. The checks are ordered so that a source that isn't a dictionary is rejected first. ::: {#55a53df7 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb class ColumnRulesAdapter(pb.ContractAdapter): format_name = "column_rules" @staticmethod def detect(source): return isinstance(source, dict) and isinstance(source.get("column_rules"), list) for source in [{"column_rules": []}, {"column_rules": "id"}, {"fields": []}, "rules.txt"]: print(f"{source!r:<24} {ColumnRulesAdapter.detect(source)}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` {'column_rules': []} True {'column_rules': 'id'} False {'fields': []} False 'rules.txt' False ``` ::: ::: Only the first source has a `column_rules` list, so it's the only one that this adapter would claim. ### [import_contract()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Read a source in this format and translate it into Pointblank terms. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/adapters/_base.py#L975-L1062){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature import_contract( source, **kwargs, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} This is the method that [`import_contract()`](`pointblank.import_contract`) calls once it has picked the adapter. It receives the source and any options the user passed, and it must return a [`ContractImport`](`pointblank.ContractImport`). An implementation usually does four things: 1. loads the content if `source` is a file path (and records the path as `source_path`) 2. collects the columns as `(name, dtype)` tuples, using Pointblank type names such as `"Int64"` and `"String"`, or `None` for a type that has no equivalent 3. translates each rule it understands into a [`MappedConstraint`](`pointblank.adapters.MappedConstraint`) that names a [`Validate`](`pointblank.Validate`) method and its arguments 4. adds a message to `warnings` for each rule it recognizes but can't translate, and sets `coverage` to the share of recognized rules that were translated Format-specific options, such as which table of a multi-table document to use, arrive in `**kwargs`. Follow the built-in adapters and raise `FileNotFoundError` for a missing file and `ValueError` for content that can't be imported. The base class version raises `NotImplementedError`, so an adapter that doesn't implement this method should set `supports_import = False`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The `source=` value given to `import_contract()`, typically a file path string or a dictionary. [**kwargs]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Any other keyword arguments given to `import_contract()`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ContractImport]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The columns, constraints, metadata, warnings, and coverage of the import. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} This adapter reads a list of column rules, where each rule has a column name and an optional lower bound. A `table=` option sets the title. ::: {#3c193af3 .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb from pointblank.adapters import MappedConstraint class ColumnRulesAdapter(pb.ContractAdapter): format_name = "column_rules" supports_export = False def import_contract(self, source, **kwargs): constraints = [ MappedConstraint( "col_vals_ge", {"columns": rule["column"], "value": rule["min"]}, f"{rule['column']} >= {rule['min']}", ) for rule in source["column_rules"] if "min" in rule ] return pb.ContractImport( source_format=self.format_name, columns=[(rule["column"], None) for rule in source["column_rules"]], constraints=constraints, metadata={"title": kwargs.get("table", "")}, ) rules = {"column_rules": [{"column": "age", "min": 0}, {"column": "name"}]} imported = ColumnRulesAdapter().import_contract(rules, table="people") imported.constraints ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ``` [MappedConstraint('col_vals_ge', columns='age', value=0)] ``` ::: ::: Calling the method on an instance, as done here, is a handy way to test an adapter. Once the class is registered with [`register_adapter()`](`pointblank.register_adapter`), the same import is available as `pb.import_contract(rules, format="column_rules", table="people")`. ### [export_contract()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Translate a Pointblank contract or validation into this format. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/adapters/_base.py#L1064-L1156){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature export_contract( validation_or_contract, destination=None, **kwargs, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} This is the method that [`export_contract()`](`pointblank.export_contract`) calls once it has picked the adapter. It receives the object to export, the optional destination, and any options the user passed. It should build the document, write it to `destination` when one is given, and return it in either case. The object can be a [`Contract`](`pointblank.Contract`) or a [`Validate`](`pointblank.Validate`) object. A contract is the easier of the two to work from: its `name`, `description`, `schema` (a [`Schema`](`pointblank.Schema`) whose `columns` attribute is a list of `(name, dtype)` tuples), and `steps` (a list of [`Step`](`pointblank.Step`) objects, each with a `method` and `kwargs`) map naturally onto most schema formats. Steps that have no equivalent in the format are usually left out. An adapter that only handles some kinds of object should raise `TypeError` for the others. The built-in adapters return a dictionary, which suits JSON and YAML formats, but a string is fine for text-based formats. The base class version raises `NotImplementedError`, so an adapter that doesn't implement this method should set `supports_export = False`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [validation_or_contract]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The `Contract` or `Validate` object given to `export_contract()`. [destination]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The file path to write to, or `None` to only return the document. [**kwargs]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Any other keyword arguments given to `export_contract()`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [str | dict]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The exported document. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} This adapter exports a contract as a list of column rules, writing a lower bound for each `col_vals_ge()` step and leaving out every other kind of step. ::: {#1d853265 .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb class ColumnRulesAdapter(pb.ContractAdapter): format_name = "column_rules" supports_import = False def export_contract(self, validation_or_contract, destination=None, **kwargs): if not isinstance(validation_or_contract, pb.Contract): raise TypeError("Only a Contract can be exported as column rules.") rules = [ {"column": step.kwargs["columns"], "min": step.kwargs["value"]} for step in validation_or_contract.steps if step.method == "col_vals_ge" ] doc = {"column_rules": rules} if destination is not None: with open(destination, "w") as f: f.write(repr(doc)) return doc contract = pb.Contract( name="people", steps=[ pb.Step("col_vals_ge", columns="age", value=0), pb.Step("col_vals_not_null", columns="name"), ], ) ColumnRulesAdapter().export_contract(contract) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ``` {'column_rules': [{'column': 'age', 'min': 0}]} ``` ::: ::: Only the `col_vals_ge()` step was written, since the format has no way to express a not-null rule. After registering the class with [`register_adapter()`](`pointblank.register_adapter`), the same export is available as `pb.export_contract(contract, format="column_rules")`.
